evidence.quote: Outbound access is limited to the sidecar's default allowlist unless the `network` permission scope allows more.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: rivet.dev/pricing (2026-11-08): "one control plane node in one availability zone, up to 1 Actor Node at no charge (R-5 or R-10)"; "designed for prototyping". Max 1/2 vCPU / 2 GB, so it is left out of pricing.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: $10/mo control plane (one node, one availability zone) plus Actor Nodes. Up to 3 Actor Nodes, R-5 to R-20. Email support.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $120/mo control plane (three nodes across three availability zones) plus Actor Nodes. Up to 10 Actor Nodes, all sizes up to R-160. Slack and email support. YC and a16z Speedrun companies get 50% off Team for 12 months (not modelled).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: $900/mo control plane (five nodes across three availability zones) plus Actor Nodes. Up to 50 Actor Nodes. Dedicated support. More nodes or larger sizes: contact sales.

caveats: Two products on one bill: agentOS (V8 isolates + WebAssembly, persistent /home/agentos filesystem, Bash/Node/Python) and Rivet Actors (stateful Node/Bun processes). Both run on the Actor Nodes of your cluster.

Price = monthly control plane (Free $0, Hobby $10, Team $120, Enterprise $900) plus a monthly price per Actor Node: R-5 1/4 vCPU 1 GB $4.20 up to R-160 8 vCPU 16 GB $94.50 (rivet.dev/pricing, 2026-11-08). The pricing page lists no per-second, storage or egress rates.

Node caps by plan: Free 1, Hobby 3, Team 10, Enterprise 50; R-40 and R-160 need Team or higher. More nodes: contact sales. At 4 vCPU / 8 GB per machine, the published caps fit about 10 machines on Team and 50 on Enterprise.

Many light actors share one node, so the cost per agent can be much lower than one node per machine. Actors per node and proration are not published; the price here assumes one node per machine of your size for the whole month.

An isolate is not a Linux machine: no Docker, no root, no apt or arbitrary binaries inside agentOS (registry only). For those, Rivet documents mounting an external sandbox (E2B, Daytona, Freestyle, or your own Docker) into the VM; that sandbox is billed by its provider, not by Rivet.
Coding agents: Rivet Agents runs Pi natively. Claude Code and Codex run through a sandbox adapter (E2B by default, or Daytona); "agentOS can't run Claude Code" (rivet.dev/guides/run-claude-code/).
Free plan is capped at one R-5 or R-10 node (max 1/2 vCPU), so it is left out of pricing.
Self-hosting the open-source stack (Apache 2.0) has no Rivet fee; "Bring your own nodes ... at no extra cost beyond the control plane."
Clusters run on Google Cloud in the region you pick: us-east4, us-central1, europe-west1, europe-west3, asia-southeast1, asia-east1.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited.

fleet.tiers: Actor Nodes per cluster: Free 1, Hobby 3, Team 10, Enterprise 50 (rivet.dev/pricing). Largest node R-160 = 8 vCPU / 16 GB. More nodes: contact sales.
fleet.notes: Caps are on nodes, not on actors; actors per node are not published. Team caps the cluster at 10 x R-160 = 80 vCPU / 160 GB; Enterprise at 50 x R-160 = 400 vCPU / 800 GB.

snapshot_auto.quote: agentOS persists the `/home/agentos` filesystem, durable session catalog, and completed session history across actor sleep. A later client call wakes a fresh VM. Adapter processes, running commands, shells, live subscriptions, and in-progress ACP deltas do not survive VM shutdown.
snapshot_auto.note: Actor sleeps after idle timeout (RivetKit default 30 s) and the VM shuts down; /home/agentos lives in the actor's SQLite and is continuously persisted (this is persistent_disk, not a snapshot). Running processes, shells and in-memory mounts are explicitly lost; the agent session is restored lazily via ACP session/resume or session/load on next prompt.

harness_api.quote: While a run is in progress, `prompt(text, { whenBusy })` decides what happens to the new prompt: ... "steer" | The agent reads the message after its current tool calls finish, before its next model call. ... To cancel a run, call `conversation.abort(id)`.
harness_api.note: First-party sessions API in Rivet Agents (agents run as Actors): prompt with whenBusy followUp/steer/reject, conversation.abort(id), conversation.compact(id), streamed events, multiple conversations per agent. The former agentOS pages (agentos/docs/agents/claude.md, agentos/docs/sessions.md) now return 404.

egress_allowlist.quote:
network: {
		default: "deny",
		rules: [
			{
				mode: "allow",
				operations: ["*"],
				patterns: ["dns://api.example.com", "tcp://api.example.com:*"],
egress_allowlist.note: Default: "outbound network access is limited to the sidecar's default allowlist" (not a flat deny); the `network` scope can be "allow", "deny", or a rule set with a default mode and dns://host / tcp://host:port patterns, enforced by the trusted sidecar outside the guest. IP/CIDR patterns are not documented, so level = domain (ports also filterable). Set by the host config, not by the guest.

egress_http_rules.quote: A scope can be `"allow"`, `"deny"`, or a rule set with a `default` mode and `rules` that match operations and target patterns.
egress_http_rules.note: Network rules match dns:// and tcp://host:port patterns only; no method/path/header rules documented. Custom HTTP-level mediation would have to be built with host functions.

ingress_rules.quote: Hosted VMs can expose any port through an expiring preview. A preview is a signed URL path that proxies HTTP to a port inside the VM until it expires or is revoked. `config.preview.defaultTtlMs` sets the default lifetime.
ingress_rules.note: Guest listeners and loopback traffic stay inside the VM; exposure is per port via signed, expiring, revocable previews served through the VM gateway with a token (e.g. a scoped JWT). Lifetime set by config.preview.defaultTtlMs or per-preview ttlMs; no maximum lifetime is stated. Server-to-server access via fetch/httpRequest.

guest_firewall.quote:
It implements a focused subset of the kernel surface, so a few Linux-specific features are not available:

- Kernel modules and eBPF
guest_firewall.note: agentOS is a virtual POSIX kernel over V8 isolates + WASM, no root, no apt/arbitrary binaries (registry only); no netfilter/iptables in the virtual kernel. Network control is the host-side permission policy instead. Derived from architecture, not an explicit 'no iptables' statement.

secret_proxy.quote: Pass LLM provider keys via the `env` option on `openSession`.
secret_proxy.note: Model keys enter the VM as session env vars (and are stored plaintext in the per-VM SQLite). The alternative pattern is host functions: "Credentials ... Stay on the host. Host functions run your functions server-side; agents see only inputs and outputs" (versus-sandbox) - an RPC tool mechanism, not a transparent outbound credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Back a guest path with external storage by adding it to the `mounts` config. Each mount takes a `path` and an optional `readOnly` flag, and the guest only ever sees the mounted subtree, never the wider host.
volume_attach.note: Built-in mount plugins: host directory, S3 / S3-compatible (block-store format, 4 MB chunks), Google Drive, in-memory, external-sandbox filesystem; dynamic mountFs()/unmountFs(). Storage is the customer's own bucket/drive; Rivet sells no separate volume product. Host/remote mounts read-only by default, writable opt-in.

image_oci.quote: You cannot download and install arbitrary binaries (for example via `curl` or `apt`), and standard Linux package managers (`apt`, `yum`) are not available since agentOS runs a streamlined Linux environment rather than a full distribution.
image_oci.note: agentOS boots V8-isolate/WASM VMs from a fixed software registry, not a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image; Rivet Actors run plain Node/Bun processes, not container images either.

docker_inside.quote:
It implements a focused subset of the kernel surface, so a few Linux-specific features are not available:

- Kernel modules and eBPF
- Container runtimes (e.g. Docker)
- File watching (`inotify`, `fs.watch`)
docker_inside.note: Not inside agentOS. Rivet documents mounting an external sandbox (E2B, Daytona, Freestyle, or a Docker container on your own worker) for container workloads; that sandbox is billed by its provider.

nested_virt.quote: The VM has no access to GPUs, USB devices, or other hardware.
nested_virt.note: agentOS is itself a virtual POSIX kernel over V8 isolates + WebAssembly with no host hardware access, so /dev/kvm-style nested virtualization is not available; Actors are plain Node/Bun processes with no VM layer at all.

desktop.quote: Spin up a sandbox when the workload needs a real Linux kernel: ... GUI applications and VNC sessions
desktop.note: Not inside agentOS or Actors. Rivet points GUI and VNC work to an external sandbox from another provider, mounted into the VM and billed by that provider.

browser.quote: The page loads in a real browser in Browserbase's cloud and comes back as clean content — the VM never runs a browser.
browser.note: Not inside agentOS. Rivet's browser tool loads pages in Browserbase (a separate paid service); a full browser needs an external sandbox from another provider.

computer_use.quote: Spin up a sandbox when the workload needs a real Linux kernel: ... GUI applications and VNC sessions
computer_use.note: Not inside agentOS or Actors: there is no screen to drive. An external sandbox from another provider can supply one.

anti_bot.quote: The page loads in a real browser in Browserbase's cloud and comes back as clean content
anti_bot.note: No anti-bot feature is documented; browsing goes through Browserbase.

captcha_solving.quote: The page loads in a real browser in Browserbase's cloud and comes back as clean content
captcha_solving.note: No CAPTCHA solving is documented in Rivet; browsing goes through Browserbase.

egress_ip_type.quote: Guest outbound to host or external. Connections that do not target a VM-owned listener take the external network path: permission checks, DNS pinning, then a real host `TcpStream`.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound connections leave through Rivet's own cloud infrastructure hosts; no residential/mobile egress product is documented, so it is ordinary datacenter egress.

ssh.quote: There are no host escapes: guest code cannot spawn a real host process, touch the real host filesystem, or open a real host network socket.
ssh.note: No SSH access is documented; agentOS/Actors are reached only through the client SDK / RivetKit API, not a shell login.

snapshot.quote: agentOS persists the `/home/agentos` filesystem, durable session catalog, and completed session history across actor sleep. ... Running processes ... Active shells ... In-memory mounts | VM memory | No
snapshot.note: State survives sleep via continuous SQLite persistence of the filesystem/session catalog, but there is no documented point-in-time snapshot/restore artifact (fs or mem) that a customer can create; it is a persistence model, not a snapshot feature.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The native sidecar reads and writes filesystem chunks directly through the actor's authenticated SQLite Unix socket.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI to take an explicit on-demand snapshot/checkpoint is documented; persistence is continuous and automatic, not a customer-triggered checkpoint.

fork.quote:
Manual Lifecycle Controls
You can also trigger lifecycle transitions from the Rivet Cloud API. These endpoints are useful for operational workflows, debugging, and forcing an actor to move through the same sleep or reschedule path that the platform would normally trigger.
fork.note: Documented lifecycle controls cover sleep/wake/destroy; no clone/fork-a-machine-into-a-new-one capability is documented for Actors or agentOS VMs.

fork_running.note: No fork capability at all is documented, so cloning a running machine without stopping it is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork capability at all is documented, so a memory-preserving fork is not offered.

pause_resume.note: A manual Cloud API call can force an actor/agentOS VM to sleep; it wakes on the next request. Sleep frees node capacity; the node itself is billed per month.

volume_shared.quote: Back a guest path with external storage by adding it to the `mounts` config. Each mount takes a `path` and an optional `readOnly` flag, and the guest only ever sees the mounted subtree, never the wider host.
volume_shared.note: Mounts (host dir, S3, Google Drive, in-memory, external sandbox) are configured per-VM; no documented feature mounts one Rivet-managed volume across several running machines simultaneously.

live_resize.quote: Soft Limit: Application-level limit, configurable in RivetKit. These cannot exceed the hard limit.
live_resize.note: No documented API to change CPU/RAM of a running actor/VM without recreating it; resource sizing is set at deploy/config time.

agent_harnesses.quote: agentOS can't run Claude Code, because it only runs software from its own registry, not binaries downloaded with `curl`.
agent_harnesses.note: Rivet Agents runs Pi natively (rivet.dev/agents/docs). Claude Code and Codex have Rivet guides; each session runs in "An E2B sandbox per session, created through the sandbox adapter", or Daytona. That sandbox is billed by E2B or Daytona.

own_agent_api.quote: Bring your harness. Rivet runs existing agent harnesses, starting with Pi, instead of asking you to rewrite your agent for a new framework.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Rivet Agents runs existing third-party harnesses (Pi first), not a first-party Rivet-branded browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.quote: The hosted endpoint is `https://mcp.rivet.dev/mcp`. ... Rivet MCP uses `search` to find `rivet.actors.list`, lists the matching `chat-room` Actors, and returns one concise result.
mcp_server.note: First-party hosted and local MCP server to list/inspect/call Rivet Actors.

public_ipv4.quote: Hosted VMs can expose any port through an expiring preview. A preview is a signed URL path that proxies HTTP to a port inside the VM until it expires or is revoked. `config.preview.defaultTtlMs` sets the default lifetime.
public_ipv4.note: Machines are reached only through Rivet's proxying endpoints/preview URLs and anycast routing, not a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine.

inbound_https.quote: Hosted VMs can expose any port through an expiring preview. A preview is a signed URL path that proxies HTTP to a port inside the VM until it expires or is revoked. `config.preview.defaultTtlMs` sets the default lifetime.
inbound_https.note: Previews proxy HTTP to a port inside the agentOS VM via https://api.rivet.dev/gateway/{vm_id}@{token}/request{path}; Actors are likewise reached via HTTPS through the Rivet gateway.

static_egress_ip.quote: Guest outbound to host or external. Connections ... take the external network path: permission checks, DNS pinning, then a real host `TcpStream`.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/dedicated outbound IP product is documented for agentOS or Actors.

gpu.quote: The VM has no access to GPUs, USB devices, or other hardware.
gpu.note: Explicitly no GPU access in agentOS; no GPU machine type is offered for Actors either.

windows.quote: agentOS is a Linux environment with a POSIX-compliant virtual kernel.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — agentOS and Actors are Linux/Node-based only, no Windows machine type.

macos.quote: agentOS is a Linux environment with a POSIX-compliant virtual kernel.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machine type is documented.

hipaa.quote: Priority support & SLA. Hardening guidance for FedRAMP, HIPAA, regulated industries
hipaa.note: Rivet offers hardening guidance towards HIPAA for Enterprise BYOC/self-host, but does not state it is HIPAA-eligible or that a BAA is available on Rivet Cloud.

max_session_h.quote: Actor stop threshold | — | 30 minutes | Maximum time for an actor to stop before it is considered lost.
max_session_h.note: No hard cap on total actor/VM lifetime is documented; actors run indefinitely, sleeping when idle (RivetKit default 30 s) and waking on the next request, so there is no fixed maximum session length.

arm64.quote: Support WebSockets/HTTP via path routing – no need for headers or custom protocols - AMD64 Docker image - Coolify support added
arm64.note: Only an AMD64 Docker image is documented for running Rivet's worker/control plane (self-host/Coolify); no ARM64 build, image tag, or vCPU architecture option is published anywhere for Rivet Cloud, BYOC, or self-host. Derived from absence of any ARM64 mention across pricing, architecture, and changelog pages.

usage_api.quote: Your monthly cost is the control plane price for your plan plus your Actor Nodes.
usage_api.note: Billing is now per plan and per node, not metered. No usage or billing API is documented.

persist_scope.quote: agentOS persists the `/home/agentos` filesystem, durable session catalog, and completed session history across actor sleep.
persist_scope.note: The /home/agentos folder survives sleep; running processes, shells and in-memory mounts do not.

locations_quote: Clusters run on Google Cloud in the region you pick when creating the cluster.
